newsitem.title: IRAN: Iranian director's Cannes winner not seen in Iran. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Iranian director's Cannes winner not seen in Iran. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]

text.p: The Iranian film jointly awarded the coveted Golden Palm best film award at the Cannes film festival has not been shown in Iran, a film critic said on Monday.

Director Abbas Kiarostami's "The Taste of the Cherry", a late entry in the competition, won the prize with Japanese director Shohei Imamura's "The Eel" on Sunday at the 50th anniversary of the yearly festival.
"None of the Iranian film experts or critics have seen this film although they insisted on the director showing it to at least a limited audience," said the critic, who asked not to be named.
"But the director refused on the grounds that any judgement here might jeopardise the film's international success," he added.
Kiarostami, 52, entered the film at Cannes after Iran's Foreign Ministry intervened to overturn a ban imposed by the country's Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance.

Kiarostami said in Cannes, where he was given a standing ovation, that the culture ministry had told him he would be banned from exhibiting his film in Cannes because it should be shown first at the Fajr (Dawn) festival in Tehran in February marking the anniversary of the 1979 Islamic revolution.
"The Taste of the Cherry" is a meditation on suicide and Islam -- a controversial subject in the Islamic republic. It depicts a young soldier who refuses to help a man kill himself.

Some of Kiarostami's previous work has been controversial in Iran for dealing with sensitive material such as shortcomings of the country's school system. But his films have been released for public viewing and were well received. (Corrects to make clear the films were released for public viewing.)
